findings.where: Nav bar wordmark, "MMM INFRA" beside the arches, at both widths
findings.fault: The wordmark is set again in Libre Caslon bold capitals in cream, not in the logo's Georgia letterforms, and "Moseley Infrastructure Advisory Services" has been dropped. The logo's type has effectively been redrawn in the page's face, so the site's main mark no longer matches the logo Mark already uses.
findings.who_objects: Mark: the brief says the logo stays and is never redrawn. A returning contact who knows his logo would see a different name-plate.

findings.where: Article specimen headline "The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law" at desktop. The same happens in the handwritten pull quote at both widths.
findings.fault: At desktop the two-line article headline skips a whole ruled line between its lines, about 64 px of leading on roughly 33 px type, so it falls apart into two separate lines. The hero headline is set solid at 64/64, and the same article headline on the phone is set tight, so headings of the same rank are spaced differently. The script pull quote also takes two rules per line, so on the phone its four lines drift apart.
findings.who_objects: A reader opening one of Mark's articles: the title and quote read as loose fragments rather than one phrase. Angélique, who needs headings to come out the same every time she adds a post.

findings.where: Article specimen pull quote "Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on with a client country!", and the motion sketch title "written, steady, by hand" in the same view
findings.fault: Mark's handwriting is used for a multi-line passage of article text, two lines at desktop and four on the phone, and again for the motion-sketch title next to it. The tile's own rule is "one note per view … never body text". A long run of script is slow to read, and two script items in one view stop the hand from being a single, special note.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank reader on an article page (Read mode), who has to decode a long handwritten line. Mark, whose handwriting is meant to mark one personal note, not decorate the quote.

findings.where: Article specimen, the related lecture row "Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge / Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF", at both widths
findings.fault: The meta line wraps at awkward points: "23 April" is split from "2026 · PDF" at desktop, and on the phone it breaks into "Lecture · / 23 April / 2026 · PDF". The bold title's last line also sits right on the row's closing rule, so the descenders and underline merge with that rule.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scanning Mark's lectures, who sees a broken date and a title crowded against the line.
